official_reference.title: 2.0 - Data Product Overview - TESS Archive Documentation - MAST
official_reference.cross_check: The official documentation describes cadence QUALITY flags as bitmasks, notes that not every nonzero flag means data are unusable, and gives 0101001010111111 as a starting bitwise mask for cadences likely to be lower quality.

important_limits: The mask is a documented starting point, not a universal scientific acceptance rule; the intended science case must determine the filter.
No rows have been filtered from a model dataset because this pilot did not build one.
Non-finite TIME and PDCSAP_FLUX values require separate checks even when QUALITY is zero.
A quality mask should be configurable, versioned, recorded in the run manifest, and tested; do not silently discard data.
next_actions: Implement a pure, tested quality-mask function that preserves original rows and records counts before/after and exclusion reasons.
Test bitmask semantics with known examples and include the selected mask in each run manifest.
Keep this mask separate from the CPVS candidate-selection rule and do not use it to force catalog membership counts.
